name: tpl-chain-response-3-goal
task: Carry the box to the exit. If the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The task has two order-related commands that the clauses only partly capture. (1) 'Carry the box to the exit' needs the box in hand at the exit: Response(at_exit, holding_box) is stated correctly, but the task also commands picking up the box, which needs a hard Existence(holding_box) or an equivalent. Currently nothing forces the agent to ever pick up the box, so the machine can reach FINAL_STATES only via at_exit with holding_box, which the Response clause already implies, but the Compiler clue 'Every way to finish includes: at_exit, holding_box' confirms the finish requires holding_box; this is acceptable. (2) 'If the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move' is a consequent of a condition, so ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) hard is correct. No change is needed for the ChainResponse. The Existence(at_exit) and Response(at_exit, holding_box) are correct. However, the Response(at_exit, holding_box) clause makes the agent hold the box at the exit, which is stated by the task. Reviewing the full conjunction, the clauses match the task; accepting.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(at_exit) and Response(at_exit, holding_box) together require reaching the exit while holding the box, which is the 'carry the box to the exit' goal. ChainResponse(box_fell, holding_box) matches 'pick it up again on your very next move'. All three clauses are hard, trace to the task, and the compiler reports no redundancy.

texts: Reach the exit (carrying the box to the exit requires arriving there).
Carry the box to the exit: whenever the agent is at the exit, it holds the box on that step.
If the box falls, pick it up again on the very next step.
